newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Pudong aims for $25 bln in foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: China's Pudong aims for $25 bln in foreign funds.

text.p: China's Pudong New Area, the biggest development zone in Shanghai, aims to attract $25 billion in contracted foreign investment by the year 2000, the Business News said on Tuesday.
Foreign investment was needed to help to develop the financial sector, infrastructure, agriculture and tourism, the newspaper said.
Contracted overseas investment in the Pudong development zone, founded in 1990, topped $12 billion by the end of 1996, the official Xinhua news agency has reported.
Foreign investment would contribute 50 percent of the area's gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of the century, up from the current 35 percent, the Business News said.
The Pudong new area generated 52 billion yuan in GDP in 1996.
Pudong also plans to attract 26 billion yuan in domestic investment by 2000, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
